newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Benguela buys out diamond venture partner.
newsitem.headline: Benguela buys out diamond venture partner.

text.p: Benguela Concessions Ltd (Benguela), a diamond exploration and mining firm, said on Tuesday that it had bought out its joint venture partner BHP Minerals International Exploration in return for BHP taking a 25 percent stake in Benguela.

Benguela said that the joint venture, formed in January 1993 for the exploration and development of marine diamond deposits off the west coast of southern Africa, had been terminated with effect from May 31.

"The intention of Benguela and BHP was to rationalise their existing rights held through the joint venture, consequently BHP is exchanging its interest in the joint venture for shares held directly in Benguela," it said.
This transaction will enable Benguela to continue to explore and develop the marine diamond consessions for its own account, it said.

In terms of the agreement Benguela will acquire BHP's entire interest in the joint venture assets consisting of its 53.4 percent stake in the marine diamond concessions, all of the Diamond Fields International Ltd shares acquired on termination of the Luderitz Bay joint venture, as well as equipment and exploration results.
In return Benquela will issue to BHP 20.35 million shares, equivalent to a 25 percent shareholding in Benguela, at 5.45 rand a share.
Benguela said that the transaction should in the medium to long term not have any signficant impact on its earnings per share.

In the event that Benguela shareholders do not approve the share issue, the agreement provides for BHP to retain a 30 percent stake in the marine diamond concessions previously held by the joint venture and to buy 30 percent of the Diamond Fields International Ltd shares held by Benguela.
